title: TSM Stock: TSMC Confirms Employee Data Leak as Seller Seeks 3 Bitcoin for the Records - FinanceFeeds
content: TSMC confirmed on Thursday that data belonging to some current and former employees was posted on an external website without authorization. The company said so in a statement filed with the SEC, and sellers on two underground forums are asking 3 Bitcoin for the records, worth about $220,000 at Thursday’s price of $73,444. TSM stock closed Wednesday at $413.35, up 4.25%, after October revenue of NT$586.89 billion rose 59.7% year over year. TSM stock was quoted at $393.11 in Thursday’s premarket, down 4.90%, alongside a broad semiconductor selloff. The filing, signed by chief financial officer Wendell Huang, says the company has “found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised.” It adds that the exposed information “has been verified to match data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider.” TSMC says the leaked data is unrelated to its operations or its customers, and that it is notifying affected personnel. It is working with the cloud vendor, investigating authorities and a third-party cybersecurity firm. The company has not named the provider or said how the records left it. Form 6-K is the route that puts the disclosure in front of holders of TSM stock. Sellers on DarkForums and BreachForums claim roughly 46,000 records totaling 6.9GB and have threatened to publish everything if nobody buys within a week, according to Business Next. The asking price converts to about NT$7.4 million by local media calculation, and Taiwan News carried the confirmation the same day. A sample file named tsmc.txt holds 499 entries with 19 fields each. The fields cover name, date of birth, job title, nationality, national ID number, home address, mobile number, email, bank information and the phone number and address of an emergency contact. Those fields come from the sellers rather than from TSMC, which has confirmed the leak without specifying what it contained. If the sample is authentic, the exposure reaches relatives listed as emergency contacts who never worked at the company, which widens the affected population well past the headcount behind TSM stock. TSMC’s filing places the data inside a cloud vendor’s systems and outside its own, so the financial exposure behind TSM stock is a liability question about outsourced processing rather than a breach of the fabs or customer designs. Taiwan has logged five disclosed incidents in five weeks, and three of them point at an outside system. The 104 Job Bank said about 120,000 resumes were read without authorization on 6 October. 91APP reported exposure of order data for 1,329 brands and roughly 4.79 million consumers on 16 October, after an unpatched flaw in the third-party tool Appsmith. E.Sun Bank disclosed 418 accounts drained of NT$41.76 million on 3 November through an external supplier’s new banking system, and ezTravel put more than 690,000 people at risk on 9 November. TSMC is the fifth, and the smallest by headcount apart from the bank, which is why the sequence matters more to TSM stock than the count does. The same shape repeats outside Taiwan, and Coinbase denied a direct breach while confirming customer information was exposed through an analytics vendor on 3 November. DriveWealth blamed a social engineering campaign for a Revolut customer data breach, and Gnosis Pay disclosed its own customer breach on 7 November. Thursday’s decline in TSM stock arrived with Nvidia down 6.03% premarket after the Wall Street Journal reported that its board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang. Micron, Arm and Marvell had all closed higher on Wednesday, and the whole complex reversed overnight, which puts the move on the Nvidia story rather than on the leak. TSM stock is up 32.49% this year and down 8.86% over a month, on TradingView data, with a market capitalization of $1.89 trillion and a trailing price to earnings ratio of 25.52. The January to October revenue total reached NT$4,485.62 billion, up 43.3%, which is the trajectory that took TSM stock to $430 after the Q3 print. Fourth-quarter results are due around 21 January, which gives the investigation two months to produce a named vendor before management next faces questions. Article 4 of Taiwan’s Personal Data Protection Act treats a contractor that collects, processes or uses personal data on a company’s behalf as the commissioning agency. Outsourcing the processing does not transfer the obligation, so whether TSMC carries liability depends on whether either party breached the act and whether damage followed. How the two split it depends on the investigation and their contract. Article 29 puts the burden on a non-government body to prove it acted without intent or negligence. Where a victim cannot establish actual losses, courts may award NT$500 to NT$20,000 per person per incident, with a NT$200 million cap across a single event. TSMC has announced no compensation plan, and Article 34 allows qualifying public interest organizations to bring group actions, which is the route that would put a number on the TSM stock exposure. title: AI Sell-Off: Buy ANET, TSM & MU to Make Up for NVIDIA Losses - TradingView
content: The artificial intelligence (AI) trade is facing one of its toughest tests yet. After driving Wall Street's rally for much of 2026, technology and semiconductor stocks have come under intense selling pressure as investors question lofty valuations, the sustainability of hyperscaler capital expenditures and the time required to monetize massive AI investments. Rising inflation, higher Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding data-center construction have added to the pressure. The weakness is also evident in AI-focused ETFs. Over the past 30 days, the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) has declined 11.4%, while the iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) has plunged 17.1%, entering correction territory. ARTY's steeper decline indicates the extent of selling pressure across companies positioned to benefit from future AI adoption. The Nov. 5 sell-off was particularly severe. The iShares Semiconductor ETF SOXX plunged 12.1%. The pressure escalated on Nov. 8 following a corporate governance controversy involving NVIDIA NVDA. NVIDIA shares fell 4.27% on Nov. 9 as concerns over leadership continuity, board oversight and potential national-security implications weighed on investor sentiment. The sell-off deepened on Nov. 10, with NVIDIA losing another 6.5% and the Nasdaq Composite declining 1%. Broader concerns over AI infrastructure spending, complications surrounding a major Ohio data-center project and hotter-than-expected inflation further undermined technology stocks. However, does this correction signal the end of the AI investment opportunity, or is it creating an attractive entry point in fundamentally strong companies? Let's find out. Here, we have picked three AI stocks — Arista Networks ANET, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM or TSMC and Micron Technology MU — all carrying favorable Zacks Rank and having strong fundamentals, making them attractive alternatives to NVIDIA for investors seeking AI exposure beyond the market leader amid the current volatility. Why Quality AI Stocks Beyond NVIDIA Are Attractive Now Despite the correction, long-term AI infrastructure demand remains strong. According to IDC's Nov. 6 report, global AI infrastructure spending reached $121.4 billion in the second quarter, up 53.3% year over year. IDC raised its 2026 spending forecast to $521 billion from $497 billion previously and expects the market to reach $1.17 trillion by 2029. Notably, non-accelerated, CPU-based infrastructure spending grew 61.1%, outpacing the 52.2% growth in accelerated systems, highlighting expanding investment opportunities beyond GPU suppliers. Meanwhile, J.P. Morgan projected AI capital expenditure of approximately $900 billion in 2026, although financing, electricity availability and semiconductor supply remain constraints. This spending creates opportunities beyond NVIDIA across AI networking, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, high-bandwidth memory and computing processors. Investors should focus on companies translating AI demand into measurable revenue growth and stronger earnings rather than speculative AI exposure. Arista: It is benefiting from increasing demand for high-speed Ethernet networking in AI data centers. Its third-quarter 2026 revenues surged 58.5% year over year, while non-GAAP EPS increased to $1.20 from 77 cents a year earlier. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 49.1%. Management expects fourth-quarter revenues of $3.9-$4 billion. ANET's networking exposure makes it an attractive means to participate in AI infrastructure expansion beyond chip manufacturing. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings indicates growth of 45.6% on current-year sales growth of 47.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for ANET have been revised upward by 4.3% to $4.36 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. Taiwan Semiconductor: TSMC's advanced manufacturing capabilities make it indispensable to the AI semiconductor ecosystem. Its October 2026 revenues jumped 59.7% year over year. Its January-October 2026 revenues increased 43.3% to NT$4.49 trillion. TSMC offers exposure to AI demand across multiple chip designers, rather than relying on a single GPU manufacturer. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings suggests 63.9% growth, while sales are expected to increase 40.9%. Over the past seven days, 2026 earnings estimates for TSM have been revised upward by 2.3% to $17.46 per share. The stock sports a Zacks Rank #1. Micron: The AI expansion is increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced DRAM, positioning Micron favorably. The company reported strong fiscal fourth quarter 2026 revenues of $54.23 billion, compared with $11.32 billion a year earlier. Micron has also commenced high-volume shipments of HBM4. The consensus estimate for fiscal 2027 earnings suggests growth of 133.1%. Sales are expected to surge 110%. Over the past 60 days, fiscal 2027 earnings estimates for MU have been revised upward by 11.5% to $176.04 per share. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). The AI revolution has already minted millionaires. But the stocks everyone knows about aren't likely to keep delivering the biggest profits. title: TSM Stock: October Revenue Up 59.7%, Ahead of Q4 Pace - FinanceFeeds
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) reported record monthly revenue of NT$586.89 billion, approximately $17.88 billion at the exchange rate cited by InvestingCube, for October 2026. The result represents a 59.7% increase from a year earlier and a 14.7% rise from September, providing fresh evidence of strong semiconductor demand following last week’s sharp selloff in AI-related stocks. TSM stock traded at $394.19, up 1.43%, at 11:22 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, according to ChartExchange. The American depositary receipts had closed Monday at $388.62, gaining 3.51%, after a particularly volatile week that included a 10.78% decline on November 5. The October revenue figure is the first monthly reading for TSMC’s fourth quarter, which runs through December. It puts the company ahead of the average monthly revenue pace implied by its October 15 guidance of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion. The result is also relevant to investors watching Nvidia, which reports quarterly earnings on November 17. In its November 10 revenue announcement, TSMC reported October consolidated sales of NT$586.89 billion, compared with NT$511.86 billion in September and NT$367.47 billion in October 2025. The increase of approximately NT$75 billion from September pushed monthly revenue above the previous record of NT$514.81 billion set in August. October was also the first month in which TSMC generated more than NT$580 billion in sales. For January through October, consolidated revenue reached NT$4,485.62 billion, increasing 43.3% from NT$3,130.44 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. October’s 59.7% annual growth exceeded the 43.3% growth recorded over the first ten months. The acceleration is consistent with the company’s previous commentary about strong demand for leading-edge manufacturing, although the monthly release does not identify how much revenue came specifically from AI processors, smartphone chips or other products. The sequential increase is particularly notable because September had already remained close to August’s record. FinanceFeeds previously reported that TSMC’s September revenue reached NT$511.9 billion, up 54.6% year over year, leaving the company operating near its highest recorded monthly sales level. October’s result moves substantially beyond that level, suggesting that the fourth quarter has begun with stronger revenue momentum than the preceding quarter’s final month. The latest revenue number can be compared directly with the outlook management provided during its October 15 earnings announcement. In its third-quarter earnings release, TSMC projected fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, based on an exchange-rate assumption of NT$31.8 per US dollar. That guidance translates to approximately NT$1.663 trillion to NT$1.727 trillion. After October’s NT$586.89 billion, TSMC would need combined revenue of approximately NT$1.076 trillion to NT$1.140 trillion across November and December to reach the original target range. That works out to an average of roughly NT$538.1 billion to NT$569.9 billion per month over the remaining two months. October exceeded even the upper-end monthly requirement by approximately NT$17 billion. If November and December each matched October’s revenue, fourth-quarter sales would reach approximately NT$1.761 trillion, above the New Taiwan dollar equivalent of the company’s original guidance ceiling. This is a comparison using TSMC’s assumed guidance exchange rate, not a revised forecast or a confirmed earnings beat. Actual reported dollar revenue will depend on the company’s financial reporting and exchange-rate treatment during the quarter. October’s roughly $17.88 billion equivalent, calculated using a different exchange rate, should not be mixed directly with the guidance conversion. The company also forecast fourth-quarter gross margin of 65% to 67% and operating margin of 56.5% to 58.5%. Revenue alone cannot establish whether TSMC will meet those profitability targets, especially as it expands advanced manufacturing capacity. FinanceFeeds’ October 15 analysis of TSMC’s third-quarter results examined the company’s $46.72 billion quarterly revenue, 66.4% gross margin and outlook for accelerating sales. TSMC’s October figures arrive after a difficult period for semiconductor stocks. Its US-listed shares fell 10.78% on November 5, closing at $353.10, before recovering 6.33% on Friday and another 3.51% on Monday. The rebound followed concerns about AI infrastructure investment, capital spending and potential delays in data center development. Those concerns had weighed on several companies involved in advanced computing, even as their reported financial performance remained strong. TSMC’s monthly sales figures provide a more direct indication of manufacturing activity. The company produces advanced processors for customers including Nvidia, AMD and Apple, while also supplying chips for custom AI accelerators and other high-performance computing applications. Its third-quarter technology mix showed the growing importance of advanced production nodes. Chips manufactured using 2-nanometer technology accounted for 8% of wafer revenue, while 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer processes contributed 33% and 28%, respectively. Technologies at 7 nanometers and below accounted for 79% of total wafer revenue. TSMC CFO Wendell Huang said during the October earnings announcement that fourth-quarter performance would benefit from continued demand for leading-edge technologies, including the rapid expansion of 2-nanometer production. However, stronger manufacturing revenue does not necessarily establish that every AI customer is increasing its orders at the same rate. TSMC’s monthly report does not disclose customer-level sales, shipment volumes by technology or the contribution of changes in pricing. Profitability also remains a consideration. Management has previously identified margin pressure associated with the introduction of 2-nanometer technology and the higher operating costs of overseas manufacturing facilities. Investors will need the full quarterly results to determine how much of the additional revenue translates into profit. TSMC’s October revenue announcement comes one week before Nvidia’s next earnings report, making the manufacturing data particularly relevant to expectations for the AI accelerator market. Nvidia confirmed that it will release its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, with an earnings conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The reporting period ended October 25. RelatedAdvanced Micro Devices Closes at $649.42, Up 2.80%, After Lisa Su Says Supply Still Trails FinanceFeeds previously examined the upcoming announcement in its November 5 Nvidia stock analysis following the semiconductor selloff, highlighting concerns about data center construction and the durability of AI infrastructure spending. TSMC’s results provide evidence that demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing remained strong in October, but they cannot independently predict Nvidia’s revenue or earnings. The companies operate at different points in the supply chain, and manufacturing revenue does not necessarily correspond to sales recognized by Nvidia during the same reporting period. Investors will be watching Nvidia’s data center revenue, its forward guidance and management’s comments on accelerator demand, production capacity and customer spending. Those disclosures should offer another perspective on whether the industry’s strong manufacturing activity is continuing to translate into revenue growth for chip designers. For TSM stock, the next milestone will be the November revenue release, which will show whether October’s record was sustainable. November and December need to average approximately NT$570 billion to reach the upper end of the company’s existing fourth-quarter revenue target under its original exchange-rate assumption. October’s NT$586.89 billion provides a strong start and reduces the monthly revenue pace required for the remainder of the quarter. The remaining questions concern whether manufacturing demand can sustain that level and whether TSMC can preserve its projected margins while expanding its most advanced production technologies. Intel Corporation INTC and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM are two premier semiconductor manufacturers competing in advanced chip fabrication and foundry services. Both are competing hard in the AI-powered chipmaking market, with Intel expanding its foundry business and TSM dominating the contract chipmaking market.Intel is currently focusing on AI chips for data centers and PCs, which marks one of the largest architectural shifts for the company in 40 years. The decision is primarily aimed at gaining a firmer footing in the expansive AI sector, spanning cloud and enterprise servers to networks, volume clients and ubiquitous edge environments, in tune with the evolving market dynamics. The foundry operating model is a key component of the company's strategy and is designed to reshape operational dynamics and drive greater transparency, accountability and focus on costs and efficiency. TSM is benefiting from accelerating AI investments, growing demand for advanced semiconductor technologies and aggressive global manufacturing expansion. The company's technological leadership, strong profitability and robust demand outlook position it favorably for sustained growth.Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends. Intel is witnessing healthy traction in AI PCs that have taken the market by storm. Its innovative AI solutions are set to benefit the broader semiconductor ecosystem by driving down costs, improving performance and fostering an open, scalable AI environment. The proliferation of generative AI applications is driving significant investments in data center infrastructure. Although GPUs remain at the center of AI computing, CPUs continue to play an important role in supporting AI workloads. This is creating incremental opportunities for Intel's Xeon portfolio. The momentum is encouraging as AI-related infrastructure spending is likely to remain healthy, providing Intel with an opportunity to capitalize on rising compute requirements. Intel is ramping Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake products based on its advanced 18A process technology. Increasing adoption of these products, coupled with an eventual enterprise PC refresh cycle, should support the client business over the long run. The company is also expanding its presence in edge computing and physical AI applications, including robotics. These emerging markets could broaden Intel's addressable opportunity beyond traditional PCs. However, Intel derives a significant part of its revenues from China. As Washington tightens restrictions on high-tech exports to China, Beijing has intensified its push for self-sufficiency in critical industries. This shift poses a dual challenge for Intel, as it faces potential market restrictions and increased competition from domestic chipmakers. The company is also lagging in the GPU and AI front compared to peers, such as NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD. Leading technology companies are reportedly piling up NVIDIA's GPUs to build computing clusters for their AI work, driving exponential revenue growth. TSM remains a key beneficiary of accelerating investments in AI infrastructure. Growing demand for AI accelerators, custom chips, networking processors and agentic AI applications is driving the adoption of its advanced manufacturing technologies. TSM's leadership in cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing provides a significant competitive advantage. Management expects N2-family annual capacity to more than double in 2027, supported by robust smartphone and HPC/AI demand. Its next-generation A14 technology remains on track for risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028, strengthening long-term growth opportunities. TSM is accelerating manufacturing investments to capitalize on sustained semiconductor demand. The company reiterated its 2026 capital expenditure budget of $60-$64 billion and expects investments during 2026-2028 to significantly exceed those of the preceding three years. The company is developing nearly 20 fabrication facilities globally. Its second Arizona fab is scheduled to begin volume production in the third quarter of 2027, while an additional 3-nanometer capacity in Taiwan is expected to become operational during 2027 and 2028. These investments should strengthen supply capabilities and support future revenue growth.However, TSM faces headwinds from rising manufacturing costs, significant capital expenditure requirements and ongoing global capacity expansion. The expansion of overseas manufacturing facilities, particularly in the United States, is expected to increase gross margin dilution to 3-4 percentage points over the next few years, compared with approximately 2 percentage points anticipated for 2026. Elevated spending could constrain free cash flow generation and weigh on returns if demand growth fails to keep pace with capacity additions. Moreover, rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties are pressuring consumer-oriented and price-sensitive end markets, prompting management to adopt a cautious approach toward 2027 business planning. These factors could limit near-term margin expansion and profitability despite robust demand for advanced semiconductor technologies.
